reforms.description: The Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 (EISA) revised the Renewable Fuels Standard (RFS) to increase the use of bio-fuels and set mandatory life-cycle GHG emissions thresholds. Additionally, the American Reinvestment and Recovery Act of 2009 significantly increased public funding for Research, Development, and Deployment (RD&D) to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, allocating approximately USD 26.7 billion, with a focus on energy efficiency and advanced energy technologies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The reforms aim to enhance energy efficiency and promote the use of renewable energy sources, which are expected to contribute positively to economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Both reforms have been enacted and are currently in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: Both reforms represent significant policy changes aimed at enhancing energy innovation and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
reforms.source_quote: The Administration gave a substantial boost to public funding for Research, Development and Deployment (RD&D) to reduce GHGemissions through the American Reinvestment and Recovery Act of2009 (ARRA), which boosted such funding by about USD26.7 billion.

reforms.description: Cuts to employer social security contributions for hiring workers unemployed more than 60 days were passed in the United States in March 2010, aimed at reducing unit labour costs and boosting hiring.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The reform is designed to incentivize hiring, which can lead to increased employment and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform was passed and is currently in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: While the reform is not a major overhaul, it represents a significant adjustment aimed at improving employment conditions.
reforms.source_quote: Cuts to employer social security contributions for hiring workers unemployed more than 60 days, with additional incentives if those workers remain employed a year later, as passed in the United States in March 2010, should also reduce unit labour costs and help boost hiring.

reforms.description: The DOE plans to double investment in basic research over the next five years, focusing on energy sciences and various energy technologies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Doubling investment in basic research is expected to foster innovation and technological advancements in energy sciences.
reforms.status_evidence: The plan has been announced but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant commitment to enhancing the foundational research necessary for future energy technologies.
reforms.source_quote: The government plans to double investment in basic research over the next five years.
